turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México reports Baja California Sur ended October with 1.1 percent fewer formal jobs than a year earlier.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: While the country as a whole reached a new IMSS record. That contrast lingers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias says Los Cabos business owners are watching the Camina Cabo walkability plan stay paused at the state level.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No word on when the downtown Cabo San Lucas makeover might move again. [pause] What happens to those empty storefronts in the meantime?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They point to shops closing or leaving for El Tezal. The association wants answers from urban development officials.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The economy guide lists constant GDP at 187,152 million pesos for 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That figure sits there like a quiet anchor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Up 3.5 percent from the year before, yet the local job count drifts the other way.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the numbers point in different directions. [chuckle] What does a paused plan teach a place about its own growth?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today we are chasing one question: what does a paused plan teach a place about its own growth?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México reports that Baja California Sur ended October with 1.1 percent fewer formal jobs than a year earlier.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. That lands differently when you picture someone checking the IMSS count at month end.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The state had 224,460 registered jobs in September.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 1,539 fewer than the year before. Who feels that first?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It marks another consecutive month of annual decline for the state.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert light falls on empty desks now. What does that quiet look like in a family kitchen?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile the rest of Mexico reached a record 23.09 million IMSS jobs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The contrast makes the local number stand out more. What does a lost job look like here?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It makes you wonder how the state can feel so separate from the national trend.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Now the stalled projects. Meganoticias says Los Cabos business owners are frustrated that the state has paused the Camina Cabo pedestrian plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the downtown Cabo San Lucas makeover too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Both had Fiturca money. The association says there is no explanation and downtown is declining as shops close or move to El Tezal.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A street that was meant to invite people to walk now stays quiet. What would you ask the officials?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They plan to request a new review with urban development officials.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One plan on hold can ripple through many small leases. [pause] I keep wondering how the sidewalks feel without footsteps.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The association points to businesses closing or moving north to El Tezal as proof of the decline.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Further north, NTCD covered a different story.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The quiet one.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The National Employment Service delivered 48,000 pesos in equipment to eight micro-entrepreneurs in Loreto and Mulegé.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One in Loreto and seven across Santa Rosalía, Guerrero Negro, Isla Natividad and San Ignacio.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Small tools and machines so family businesses can start or keep going.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 48,000 pesos is not much in a state budget, yet it reaches eight doorsteps.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: While formal employment slips in the south, these grants land in the north.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Different scales, same question of what holds a place together. [chuckle] The road south always surprises you that way.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The business owners in Los Cabos want their review restarted.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the eight families just want the tools to open tomorrow.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Two ends of the same coast.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What stays when the big plans pause and the small ones keep moving?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It feels like the coast itself is holding both the pause and the quiet forward motion at once.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. The swell keeps coming in even when the big plans sit on a desk.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos holds the biggest share of the story right now, with 351111 people spread across 428 localities.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That number feels heavy when you stand on the corridor and watch the hotels line the coast.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The airport and the hospitality cluster keep pulling everything south.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the same place reports water aquifers 0317 and 0319 already in deficit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does daily life feel like when the desal plants run at peak just to keep the lights on in those rooms?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México notes the state lost 1.1 percent of formal jobs year on year by October.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One point one percent down while the rest of the country added work.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: September sat at 224460 registered jobs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That number lands differently when you picture someone closing a shop on the Cabo San Lucas waterfront.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reports the business association says the Camina Cabo plan and the downtown makeover have simply stalled at the state level.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No explanation, just paused.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They mention shops drifting out to El Tezal instead.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering what a worker in one of those stalled projects would ask the officials if they could sit down together.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz carries its own weight with 292241 residents.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Its poverty rate sits lowest among the municipalities at 20.6 percent back in 2020.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its revenue sits at 2905974532 pesos for 2026.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Still, the Todos Santos aquifer 0313 runs in deficit while lifestyle migration keeps arriving.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the families moving into that Pacific spine about the road and the coast they now share?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The luxury resorts keep opening, Auberge properties, Nobu, Montage, all along the same corridor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the service capacity and the water stay the quiet limit behind the brand. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about the families in Todos Santos watching the highway fill with new cars each season, wondering how the septic systems will hold when the rain comes light again. [pause] What would the fishers in the old harbor ask about the water they share now with the new homes?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The desert teaches the city to move slower than the money wants to go.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The revenue law for Los Cabos next year caught my eye.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports the council sent congress a plan for 6,746 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is nine percent below this year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Own-source revenue drops nearly 20 percent because property and transfer taxes are slowing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Real estate cooling seems to be the thread pulling at everything else.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's earlier Foresight notes the same coastal pressure from El Niño and extreme tides.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: HOY BCS covered the partial demolition of Hotel San Cristóbal at Punta Lobos after waves undercut the foundations.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fishers warned about the Tres Santos development changing the beach since 2015.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No official technical report yet on what exactly shifted the sand.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the market that feeds the budget is literally being washed away. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Sea of Cortez Forum keeps asking how the region can double its economy without crossing those limits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile the governor is promising solar panels and road loops to the ranch communities around La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Palabra BCS says those fixes reach Texcalama and San Andrés by January.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He also mentioned a roughly 50 km loop called La Herradura de la Sierra.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That feels like a quiet shift away from the coast.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the knowledge graph still shows no firm list of battery storage projects or their megawatts.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without that storage the solar on the ranches stays small.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same graph lists two big mining projects that were canceled years ago.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cardones and Don Diego both lost their permits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Don Diego even left an ICSID award of 37.1 million dollars hanging in the air.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the economy keeps circling back to the same fragile strip of sand.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fishers in Cabo San Lucas are now preparing an amparo against the new port fees.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Peninsular Digital says the Mar Azul cooperative never got consulted.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One more sign the infrastructure underneath the numbers is starting to crack.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But the rural solar commitments might be the surprise thread that holds longer.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. The desert teaching the city how to stay. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The gas leak at the Infra plant shows another side of the same story.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México reported the high-pressure release forced a school evacuation in Pueblo Nuevo.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They have visited the site several times before, the fire chief said.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Because homes and schools now surround it, relocation is under review.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Hurricane Polo brought seven shelters open across Loreto from Agua Verde to San Nicolás.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 60 Navy and 30 Defense personnel helped while commerce stopped for the day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Does the desert teach us to build lighter on the land?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Or perhaps the sea keeps reminding us where the real edge lies. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Foresight keeps circling back to those coastal limits year after year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the rural solar and the quiet roads might still be the thread that lasts. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know that labor poverty here sits at just 13.2 percent, the lowest of any state in Mexico?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Thirteen point two. That number feels small next to the usual headlines.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: CON EVAL tracked it at the end of 2024. It means fewer working people here struggle to cover basic food and housing than anywhere else.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Imagine a cook in Cabo San Lucas finishing a shift. Her wage still buys the same tortillas and fish it did last year, while prices elsewhere keep climbing.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The economy grew 3.5 percent in constant pesos that same year, reaching 187,152 million, according to INEGI.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Three point five. Slow and steady, like the tide coming in rather than a sudden swell.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It lines up with the last decade’s average of 2.1 percent a year that Agustín Coppel mentioned at the Sea of Cortez Forum.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet formal jobs dipped 1.1 percent year on year by October, per IMSS data cited in Tribuna de México.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 224,460 posts stood in September. Not a collapse, just a pause.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach a city when the numbers move like this?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It teaches patience. The same 3.5 percent growth target Coppel set for the whole region over 20 years starts to feel possible.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: IMCO noted BCS climbed from eighth to fifth in state competitiveness over those same years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fifth. That shift shows up in new roads and ports the forum kept circling back to.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Foreign investment reached 1,353 million dollars in 2024 and climbed again the next year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 1,578 million dollars in 2025. Still, water keeps deciding how far any new hotel can stretch.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: If the tide brings both growth and the occasional breach in the levee, maybe the real work is learning which walls to raise and which to leave open.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. And keeping that 13.2 percent number from drifting back up when the next high tide arrives.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A quiet kind of strength, really.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The kind you notice only when you compare it to everywhere else. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What if the quiet thing deciding whether a hotel rises here is not the view but one page from CONAGUA.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The DMA balance for each aquifer. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. One everyday number that sits behind the whole viability package.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Hotel, desaladora, road, housing, energy all checked against that sheet before anything moves.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: For aquifer 0313 Todos Santos the figure reads minus 2.964513 hm³ per year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A deficit that forces the next question in the package. Really, how does that land with the families nearby?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can the desaladora close the gap without shifting pressure to another basin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Nearby, aquifer 0314 El Pescadero shows a small positive of 0.107682 hm³ per year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That contrast travels straight into the family consultations the ontology describes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The World Bank 2009 report frames it as density, distance and division all at once. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the pipe from sea to hotel carries more than water.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It carries the legal balance that families and mesas must still approve.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Michael Storper's book calls these the keys that make regions diverge.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One project either tightens or loosens the whole network of rules.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The OECD paper on rural-urban links shows how the hinterland feels that choice too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A single deficit number travels inland along the carretera.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach a city when the water account stays negative.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It teaches that every new connection changes the distance between place and permission.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Even rejected mines like Don Diego leave a 37.1 MDD award that still shapes future permits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The gap in BESS storage locations adds another layer the viability packet must weigh.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Aura III already runs at 10.5 MW, yet the larger plan calls for 63 MW more along the coast.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Wait, so that extra storage sits right beside the desaladora question families keep raising.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly, and the long road south to Comondú feels every delay in that packet.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the next mesa when the numbers finally reach the table. [laugh]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the design stays invisible until the next family sits down with the packet.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal’s visión for economy points to a polycentric path instead of one repeated coastal formula.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes, and the riesgo section notes that growth is uneven and much of the investment story remains a proposal rather than a measured path.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: INEGI shows constant-price GDP at 187,152 million pesos in 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Up how much from the year before?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Up 3.5 percent.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That sits next to the FDI numbers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CNIE recorded 1,353 million USD in 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the following year?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 1,578 million.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet formal IMSS employment slipped 1.1 percent year-on-year by October.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: With 224,460 posts in September.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the aspiration is a regenerative economy where investment is not locked only to cloning the Cabos engine.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it take for each region to keep its own role without one swallowing the others?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The tendencia 2050 describes Los Cabos under water and power stress.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape stays in tension with protected areas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz acts as the service capital and water-energy node.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Comondú keeps headroom as an agricultural hub, while northern Mulegé holds a remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That spread of distinct vocations is what the portal’s demand-supply board still sees as constrained at state scale. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The levers suggest giving real weight to La Paz as services capital, Comondú for production, and the north for remote energy rather than amenity residential without evidence.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And to read formal employment and inflation together with the water and grid ceilings.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The conditions are clear: new growth only where water and energy show evidenced margin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto respect ANP and POEL ceilings first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Forum goals like tripling FDI stay outside the portal’s own projections.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: On the watchlist sits the 2027 budget package of 28.3 billion pesos, with approval expected in December.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The fifth report was delivered to Congress on 12 November.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A public event is set for 27 November at Plaza de la Reforma in La Paz. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: If the polycentric map holds, what changes in how the state measures success year by year?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: We would track each node’s contribution instead of one headline growth figure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert and the sea already draw different lines on the map.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the question becomes whether the budget and the grid can follow those same lines.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: After everything we have heard, one question keeps turning in my mind.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Which one?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What the economy actually touches when it is not trying to copy the same shoreline again and again.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. They land where the coast feels far away, near the ranches and the places that need water and light most.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The places that feel farther away, where a single choice about a road or a panel might ripple outward.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. The ones the light reaches differently, where decisions might land closer to the ground and hold for longer.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep picturing water moving inland, and light, and a few small decisions made together, away from the cooling real estate edge.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: —which is the strange part. It could change how the whole shape feels, like roots spreading under the desert instead of towers along the sand.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Wider, like the desert itself, steady even when one part slows.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the economy becomes something that holds steady even when the coast cools, a quiet network instead of one loud engine.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] Quieter, maybe, but steadier, and more our own.
